title: Projection identities and Frobenius factorization for arbitrary finite-field models
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $q=p^a$, $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and $k$ is its fixed algebraic closure. Let $T_0$ be any $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base], with no finite-type or separatedness hypothesis. Put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change], with projections $\pi:T\to T_0$ and $\rho:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $F_0=F_{T_0}^{(q)}$ and $F=F_T^{(q)}$ be the absolute $q$-power Frobenii [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. The morphism $F_0$ is over $k_0$; hence its base change $\Phi=F_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$ is defined. Put $\sigma(z)=z^q$, $\gamma=\sigma^{-1}$ as in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and $g_\epsilon=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon=\sigma,\gamma$, using the spectrum functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then
$$
 \pi F=F_0\pi,\quad \rho F=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho,\quad
 \pi\Phi=F_0\pi,\quad \rho\Phi=\rho,\quad
 \pi g_\sigma=\pi,\quad \rho g_\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho,
$$
and the following equalities hold as scheme morphisms:
$$
 F=g_\sigma\Phi=\Phi g_\sigma,\qquad
 \Phi=g_\gamma F=Fg_\gamma,\qquad
 g_\sigma g_\gamma=g_\gamma g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_T.
$$
Here composition is written right to left. For any morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ of arbitrary $k_0$-schemes and its base change $f:X\to Y$, the corresponding endomorphisms satisfy $f\Phi_X=\Phi_Yf$ and $fF_X^{(q)}=F_Y^{(q)}f$.

proof.text: Every scheme $Z$ over $k_0$ has characteristic $p$: the structure morphism gives a unital ring map $k_0\to\mathcal O_Z(Z)$, followed by restriction to $\mathcal O_Z(U)$ for any open $U$, and these maps send $p\cdot1=0$ to $p\cdot1=0$. This applies to $T_0,T$, to $\operatorname{Spec}k_0,\operatorname{Spec}k$, and later to $X_0,Y_0,X,Y$. Thus all absolute Frobenii used below are defined, including when a scheme is empty.

source.place: Tag 03SM, definition-absolute-frobenius, characteristic-p hypothesis; inherited along the structure morphism

proof.text: For any morphism $h:Z\to W$ between these characteristic-$p$ schemes, the absolute $q$-power Frobenii satisfy $hF_Z^{(q)}=F_W^{(q)}h$. Indeed both composites have underlying continuous map $h$, and for every open $V\subseteq W$ and $s\in\mathcal O_W(V)$ their maps on sections are $(h^\sharp_V(s))^q$ and $h^\sharp_V(s^q)$, which agree since $h^\sharp_V$ is a ring homomorphism. Equality of both components gives equality as scheme morphisms. This is the full sectionwise proof of the iterated form of Stacks Tag 0CC7, not an appeal to an uncited naturality theorem.

source.place: Tag 0CC7, lemma-frobenius-endomorphism-identity, proof; same ring-homomorphism calculation with exponent q

proof.text: Write $t_0:T_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ for the structure morphism. By [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card], $c^q=c$ for every $c\in k_0$. The affine description of absolute Frobenius and functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ therefore give $F_{\operatorname{Spec}k_0}^{(q)}=\operatorname{id}$. Step 2 applied to $t_0$ gives $t_0F_0=t_0$, so $F_0$ is over $k_0$. On $\operatorname{Spec}k$, the same affine description gives $F_{\operatorname{Spec}k}^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$, since $\sigma(z)=z^q$. Applying Step 2 to $\pi$ and $\rho$ gives $\pi F=F_0\pi$ and $\rho F=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho$.

source.place: Tags 03SM and 0CC7, definition-absolute-frobenius and lemma-frobenius-endomorphism-identity; finite-field identity from the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Since $F_0$ is over $k_0$, the induced map of fibre products $\Phi=F_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$ exists and satisfies $\pi\Phi=F_0\pi$, $\rho\Phi=\rho$. The automorphisms $\sigma,\gamma$ fix $k_0$ by [def-weil-frobenius-substitution], so both $\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon)$ are morphisms over $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. The induced maps $g_\epsilon=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon)$ consequently satisfy $\pi g_\epsilon=\pi$ and $\rho g_\epsilon=\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon)\rho$ for $\epsilon=\sigma,\gamma$. These are exactly the defining projection equations of the induced maps, with no finiteness or separation assumption.

source.place: Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product; induced maps characterized by the universal property

proof.text: Use the projection equations of Steps 3 and 4. Both $g_\sigma\Phi$ and $\Phi g_\sigma$ have first projection $F_0\pi$ and second projection $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho$: for example, $\pi\Phi g_\sigma=F_0\pi g_\sigma=F_0\pi$ and $\rho g_\sigma\Phi=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho\Phi=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho$. The other two equations follow by the same substitutions, namely $\pi g_\sigma\Phi=\pi\Phi=F_0\pi$ and $\rho\Phi g_\sigma=\rho g_\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho$. These are the two projections of $F$. Uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property yields $F=g_\sigma\Phi=\Phi g_\sigma$.

source.place: absolute-Frobenius factorization display; verification using Tag 01JP projection uniqueness

proof.text: The maps $g_\sigma g_\gamma$ and $g_\gamma g_\sigma$ both have first projection $\pi$. Their second projections are respectively $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)\rho=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma\sigma)\rho=\rho$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma\gamma)\rho=\rho$, because $\gamma=\sigma^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}$ is contravariantly functorial. Fibre-product uniqueness gives $g_\sigma g_\gamma=g_\gamma g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_T$.

source.place: Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product; uniqueness applied to the inverse composites

proof.text: Associativity and Steps 5 and 6 give $g_\gamma F=g_\gamma(g_\sigma\Phi)=(g_\gamma g_\sigma)\Phi=\Phi$ and $Fg_\gamma=(\Phi g_\sigma)g_\gamma=\Phi(g_\sigma g_\gamma)=\Phi$. This proves both geometric cancellation identities.

source.place: geometric-Galois inverse convention and absolute-Frobenius factorization paragraph

proof.text: Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be any $k_0$-morphism and let $f:X\to Y$ be its base change, with projections $\pi_X,\rho_X,\pi_Y,\rho_Y$. By the defining projection equations of base change, $\pi_Yf=f_0\pi_X$ and $\rho_Yf=\rho_X$. Step 2 gives $f_0F_{X_0}^{(q)}=F_{Y_0}^{(q)}f_0$. Thus $\pi_Yf\Phi_X=f_0F_{X_0}^{(q)}\pi_X=F_{Y_0}^{(q)}f_0\pi_X=\pi_Y\Phi_Yf$, while $\rho_Yf\Phi_X=\rho_X\Phi_X=\rho_X=\rho_Y\Phi_Yf$. Fibre-product uniqueness gives $f\Phi_X=\Phi_Yf$. Finally Step 2 applied directly to $f$ gives $fF_X^{(q)}=F_Y^{(q)}f$. All the comparisons concern scheme morphisms; $F$ and $g_\epsilon$ need not be $k$-morphisms.
